source_files.role: Ported here. The file adapter: default constructor pinning /SCHEMAS/mzData_1_05.xsd and version 1.05, the three PeakFileOptions accessors, load, store and isSemanticallyValid.

Ported here. load resets the map and records the document path and type before parsing; store passes the options to the handler; isSemanticallyValid loads the hand-crafted mapping file and the psi-mzdata OBO.

Ported here. 191 lines: the two constructors, the three SAX callbacks, writeTo, setOptions, init_, fillData_, the three writeCVS_ overloads, writeUserParam_, cvParam_, writeBinary_ and the thirteen protected members.

Ported here. 1510 lines, the whole of mzData reading and writing: the 19 hard-coded cv_terms_ tables, the element dispatch, the per-array base64 decode, the cvParam_ section dispatch and the byte layout of writeTo.
The oracle. 15 START_SECTIONs, 435 assertion macros; every transcribed literal in tests/mzdata.rs comes from this file or from the three fixtures it loads.

Not ported here. Read for decodeUncompressed_ (lines 309-345), which defines the tolerances the reader must reproduce: a payload under four characters decodes to nothing, a length that is not a multiple of four throws ConversionError, and out.assign(fptr, fptr + s.size()/element_size) silently drops a trailing partial element.

Not ported here. Read for cvStringToEnum_ (lines 131-145), which resolves an unknown CV term to index 0 with a warning, and for the error/warning/fatalError triple: only fatalError throws, error logs, and warning is #ifdef'd down to a debug log in a release build.

fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream fixture and the oracle for 299 of the 435 assertion macros: accession lsid, sample MS-Sample/0-815 in the gas state, one source file, two contacts, two mass analyzers, one ion source, one ion detector, a document-wide dataProcessing with completionTime 2001-02-03T04:05:06, and three spectra at 60/120/180 s with native IDs 10/11/12, 1/3/5 peaks and eight supDataArrayBinary annotation arrays each. Hand-written, not written by OpenMS: it carries ScanFunction (PSI:1000017) and TandemScanningMethod (PSI:1000020) cvParams that writeTo never emits, and its second spectrum declares mzRangeStart without mzRangeStop, which yields the scan window (110, 0) that ScanWindow::validate rejects.

Unmodified upstream fixture: one spectrum of three peaks, both arrays precision=64 endian=little, with newlines, tabs and spaces inside the m/z base64 payload. Both payloads are 36 base64 characters, which is 25 bytes where the declared length="3" needs 24, so each depends on Base64::decodeUncompressed_ dropping the trailing partial element.

Unmodified upstream fixture and the only one that exercises endian="big": empty accessionNumber, one spectrum of three peaks with a 64-bit little-endian m/z array, a 32-bit little-endian intensity array, and eight annotation arrays mixing 32-bit little, 64-bit little, 32-bit big (QsgAAENIAABCyAAA) and 64-bit big (QFkAAAAAAABAaQAAAAAAAEBZAAAAAAAA). All eight decode to 100/200/100.

Upstream fixture deliberately NOT copied into this repository: 10.6 MB would nearly double the 15 MB of tests/data. The section's asserted value is one spectrum of 997530 peaks; tests/mzdata.rs::load_special_cases writes and reads an equivalent 997530-peak document instead. The character-data splitting the upstream comment refers to is reached directly by split_base64_payload_is_concatenated, which puts an XML comment inside a base64 payload.

Synthetic (tier 4). No upstream fixture declares endian="big" on a peak array, only on annotation arrays. One spectrum at 42 s with a 64-bit big-endian m/z array (110/120/130), a 32-bit big-endian intensity array (100/200/100) and a 32-bit big-endian annotation array named widths (1.5/2.5/3.5). byte_order_changes_the_decoded_values rewrites endian="big" to endian="little" in the same bytes and asserts the values change, which is what proves the attribute is read rather than the host byte order assumed. big_endian_input_survives_a_round_trip stores the loaded experiment back out - little endian, as writeBinary_ writes - and asserts every value returns.

Synthetic (tier 4). encoding="ISO-8859-1", which is what MzDataHandler::writeTo emits, with raw high bytes in four metadata values: sampleName Prüfmuster (0xfc), contact François Müller (0xe7, 0xfc), institution Universität Tübingen (0xe4, 0xfc) and instrumentName Meßgerät (0xdf, 0xe4). Not valid UTF-8.

Synthetic (tier 4). encoding="UTF-8" with metadata outside ISO-8859-1 (日本語, 東京, 質量分析計), so the writer has to emit numeric character references to keep its ISO-8859-1 declaration truthful. writeTo would emit the raw UTF-8 bytes under that declaration.

gates: cargo nextest run --locked --no-default-features --features mzml --test mzdata (63 tests)

source_anchors.operation: fillData_ reads precisions_[0] and precisions_[1] before the data_to_decode_.size() < 2 guard at :533, so a spectrum with fewer than two binary arrays reads past the end of a std::vector

an m/z-versus-intensity length disagreement is reported with the non-fatal error(LOAD, ...), which only logs; the loop at :558-574 then indexes the intensity array and every annotation array at every position below the m/z length

spec_.getFloatDataArrays()[i] is filled from decoded_double_list_[2 + i][n] / decoded_list_[2 + i][n] with no length check on that array, so a supDataArrayBinary shorter than the m/z array reads out of bounds

UInt count = attributeAsInt_(attributes, "count") then exp_->reserve(count): a signed Int read into an unsigned, passed straight to a reserve with no ceiling, so <spectrumList count="4000000000"> or a negative count asks for roughly a terabyte before any data is read

peak_count_ = attributeAsInt_(attributes, "length") is the only assignment to that handler member and is reached only for <data> inside <mzArrayBinary>, and onEndElement does not reset it, so a spectrum without an m/z array inherits the previous spectrum's peak count

static UInt scan_count = 0 inside onEndElement is a function-local static shared by every MzDataHandler instance and thread, so concurrent or successive loads interleave the progress count; it is reset only when </mzData> is reached

spec_.getDataProcessing().push_back(data_processing_) runs for every <spectrum> without checking the pointer, so a document with no <dataProcessing> element gives every spectrum a null DataProcessingPtr

the unknown-scan-mode fallback for an MS2 spectrum sets MSNSPECTRUM on exp_->getSpectra().back() - the previously added spectrum, and .back() on an empty vector when this is the first one - and warns only on the MS1 branch

writeTo emits <?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?> and then streams every std::string with os << unescaped and untranscoded, so an & or a < in any metadata value produces a document that is not well-formed and UTF-8 metadata produces bytes the declared encoding cannot describe
writeBinary_ hardcodes precision="32" endian="little" and encodes from the std::vector<float> data_to_encode_, so every f64 m/z coordinate loses about nine significant digits on every store

a supplemental-array length mismatch during writeTo is reported with error(LOAD, ...) rather than error(STORE, ...), so the message reads "Non-fatal error while loading" from the store path - and the misaligned array is then written anyway, producing a document whose <supDataArrayBinary> is not aligned with the peak array; fillData_ at :562-572 reads past the end of that array on the way back in
StringUtils::removeWhitespaces is applied to every payload before decoding, "this should not be necessary, but line breaks inside the base64 data are unfortunately no exception"
precision is compared only against "32" and endian only against "big", so every other spelling of either silently selects 64-bit and little endian respectively
a ScanWindow is pushed only when begin != 0.0 || end != 0.0, so a spectrumInstrument with mzRangeStart and no mzRangeStop yields the window (110, 0) whose begin exceeds its end
the decode slot for a supDataArrayBinary is pushed when its <arrayName> child opens, so an annotation array without that child shifts every following payload by one slot

init_ builds 19 cv_terms_ tables from semicolon-separated literals; five (4 ScanFunction, 12 TandemScanningMethod, 15 EnergyUnits, 16 ScanMode, 17 Polarity) are commented "no longer used" and left empty, and table 18 ActivationMethod is the only one without a leading empty entry, so cvStringToEnum_'s index-0 fallback makes an unknown activation method CID

the writer's three-flag native-ID analysis: all_prefixed_numbers takes the id from a spectrum=-prefixed number, all_numbers from a bare number, and otherwise the spectra are renumbered from 1, silently when every native ID is empty

writeTo emits PhotodiodeArrayDetector, EnhancedMultiplyChargedScan and TimeDelayedFragmentationScan for the ABSORPTION, EMC and TDF scan modes, none of which its own cvParam_ at :1088-1142 recognises, so each reads back as MASSSPECTRUM through the fallback that also touches getSpectra().back()

the data processing of the first spectrum is used for the whole document, and only <name> and <version> of its software are written - the <comments> child the reader accepts at :131-134 is never emitted, which is why MzDataFile_test.cpp:662-664 has to put the software comment back before comparing

the two constructor doc comments are swapped: the MapType& overload is documented "Constructor for a write-only handler" but assigns exp_ and is used by load, and the const MapType& overload is documented "read-only" but assigns cexp_ and is used by store

out.assign(fptr, fptr + s.size()/element_size) truncates to whole elements, so a payload holding a trailing partial element silently loses it; both MzDataFile_3_minimal.mzData and MzDataFile_4_64bit.mzData depend on this
XMLHandler::warning is #ifdef OPENMS_ASSERTIONS around OPENMS_LOG_WARN and falls back to OPENMS_LOG_DEBUG, so in a release build none of the handler's warnings reaches a user
DRange<1>::encloses is inclusive at the minimum and exclusive at the maximum, which is the membership rule every PeakFileOptions filter uses

evidence: Tier 3 source review with one independent cross-check. Every literal in tests/mzdata.rs that describes upstream data is transcribed from MzDataFile_test.cpp or from the three unmodified fixtures: 3 spectra at 60/120/180 s with native IDs spectrum=10/11/12 and 1/3/5 peaks, the eight annotation arrays area..peakShape with their URL and Comment descriptions and the supDataDesc comment bla|comment|bla, the accession lsid, two precursors at m/z 1.2 and 2.2 with charges 2 and 3 and activation CID and SID, the source file MzDataFile_test_1.raw in /share/data/, contacts John Doe and Jane Doe, dataProcessing MS-X 1.0 with completionTime 2001-02-03 04:05:06, the instrument MS-Instrument/MS-Vendor/MS 1/tuned with two analyzers at resolutions 22.33 and 12.3 and FinalMSExponent 2 and -2, the sample MS-Sample 0-815 in the gas state with mass 1.01, volume 2.02 and concentration 3.03, the 997530-peak long spectrum, and the 64-bit and mixed-endian arrays of MzDataFile_4_64bit.mzData. Transcribed literals are tier-3 evidence. The one check independent of that suite is upstream_payload_holds_a_partial_trailing_element, which decodes the m/z payload of MzDataFile_3_minimal.mzData outside the reader and shows it to hold 25 bytes where the declared three 64-bit values need 24 - establishing from the bytes, not from any upstream assertion, that the fixtures depend on Base64::decodeUncompressed_ truncating to whole elements. The big-endian, ISO-8859-1 and UTF-8 fixtures, every resource ceiling, the hostile length and count attributes, the writer refusals and the byte-exact empty-experiment document are independently derived (tier 4). No C++ was built or executed, no C++ output was retained, and no retained mzData output exists in the pinned tree - MzDataFile_1.mzData is hand-written, carrying ScanFunction and TandemScanningMethod cvParams the writer never emits - so this is not a tier 1 differential.
